needs.reason: indexing C# needs dotnet restore and build; MSBuild evaluates project files and runs their targets

traps: central package management: PackageReference carries no Version; the version is written in Directory.Packages.props, so declared comes from there and declared_in is that file, as for a catalog
Shop.Core overrides the central version with VersionOverride="8.0.10": declared is 8.0.10 and declared_in is src/Shop.Core/Shop.Core.csproj, not the 8.0.11 of Directory.Packages.props
Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore 8.0.11 in Directory.Packages.props is never used at that version: only Shop.Core references it, with the override
a NuGet version written as 8.0.3 means the minimum 8.0.3, not an exact pin
TargetFramework net8.0 sits in Directory.Build.props, not in either csproj
Shop.Api gets Entity Framework Core only through the ProjectReference: it is not a direct dependency of Shop.Api
no packages.lock.json: every resolved is null (a NuGet lock file needs a contentHash per package, not written by hand)
the solution folder 'src' in Shop.sln is a virtual folder, not a project
Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web is the evidence of ASP.NET Core: there is no PackageReference for it
